content.overview: The Constitution does not classify Directive Principles into socialist, Gandhian and liberal-intellectual groups. Those labels are a scholarly and examination map. They do not amend Article 37 and they do not decide which article applies. A safe map, used only as a study aid, places Articles 38, 39, 39A, 41, 42, 43, 43A and 47 in a social-and-economic welfare group; Articles 40, 43, 43B, 46, 47 and 48 in a Gandhian or village-and-community group; and Articles 44, 45, 48A, 49, 50 and 51 in a liberal-intellectual or administrative group. Several articles sit in more than one teaching group. The operative text remains the article itself.

sections.heading: Socialistic principles (illustrative grouping)
sections.body: Principles aimed at social and economic justice and reducing inequality — for example the policy goals reflected in Articles 38, 39, 39A, 41, 42, 43, 43A and 47. Grouping is pedagogical; each Article has its own text.

sections.heading: Gandhian principles (illustrative grouping)
sections.body: Principles associated with village organisation, cottage industry, weaker sections, and related goals — often linked in teaching materials to Articles 40, 43, 46, 47 and 48. Always return to the official Article text.

sections.heading: Liberal-intellectual principles (illustrative grouping)
sections.body: Principles associated with uniform civil code, early childhood care and education, separation of judiciary and executive, and international peace — often linked in teaching to Articles 44, 45, 50 and 51.

sections.heading: Warning
sections.body: Do not plead a classification as if it were enacted law. Plead the Article, the implementing statute, and the Part III standard if rights are claimed.

learningObjectives: State that the three-way classification is scholarly, not constitutional.
Place the principal articles in the usual teaching groups.
Apply the article text where a label and the text diverge.
enhancement.definition: The socialist, Gandhian and liberal-intellectual classification is a commentary map of Part IV. It is not enacted text and does not change Article 37.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Classification is a memory aid. Liability, legislative competence and justiciability are decided by the article and by Article 37, not by the label.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Constitution of India, Part IV. No article enacts the three labels. Article 37 remains the enforcement rule for every group.
essentialIngredients: Group used only as a teaching label
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Examination answers often sort Part IV into three labels. Socialistic or welfare articles are those aimed at livelihood, distribution of material resources, equal pay, health of workers, legal aid, work and assistance, humane conditions, maternity relief, living wage and worker participation: principally Articles 38, 39, 39A, 41, 42, 43 and 43A. Gandhian articles are those associated with village panchayats, cottage industries, cooperatives, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe interests, prohibition and agriculture or cow protection: principally Articles 40, 43, 43B, 46, 47 and 48. Liberal-intellectual articles are those on a uniform civil code, early childhood care, environment, monuments, separation of judiciary from executive, and international peace: principally Articles 44, 45, 48A, 49, 50 and 51. The map is unstable at the edges. Article 43 belongs to both the wage group and the cottage-industry group. Article 47 belongs to both nutrition and prohibition. Article 48A is often taught with the liberal group but is an environmental direction. None of these labels is a ground of challenge or a writ.
examples: A question asks for Gandhian principles. Name Articles 40, 43 cottage industries, 46, 47 prohibition and 48, and say the label is scholarly.
A student calls Article 44 socialist because it is in Part IV. The usual teaching label is liberal-intellectual; the operative text is the uniform-civil-code direction.
Article 43 is listed under two labels. The answer still quotes the living-wage and cottage-industry clauses rather than the label.
enhancement.problemApplication: Write one sentence that the classification is not text. Place each cited article. If the relief is enforcement, leave the label and apply Article 37.

keyTakeaways: The Constitution does not enact the three labels.
Social-economic, Gandhian and liberal-intellectual are teaching groups.
Articles can sit in more than one group.

verification.note: Scholarly classification kept expressly non-textual, matching the published overview. No case citation added.

content.study: Say first that the classification is not constitutional text. Then place the article the question names. Do not invent a fourth constitutional chapter. Overlap is expected: Article 43 is both a living-wage direction and a cottage-industry direction; Article 47 is both a nutrition direction and a prohibition direction.
